title: APC Smart-UPS Battery Runtime Remaining Below Safe Threshold
exclusions: Not applicable to APC units without SNMP/NMC management, third-party UPS MIBs using incompatible OID semantics, or bypass-only cabinet feeds where management cards report static placeholders during maintenance.
evidence: Retention-friendly dashboard of hourly average runtime plus the scheduled search job history tied to `index=power` events marked `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups`, exportable for facilities auditors.

app: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266), SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=power sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups host=*
| eval runtime_min=tonumber(upsAdvBatteryRunTimeRemaining)/6000
| timechart span=1h avg(runtime_min) as avg_runtime by host
| where avg_runtime < 15
description: Detects UC-15.1.26 — APC, Smart, UPS, Battery, Runtime — using `index=power` sourcetype `snmp:apc:ups`, grouped by `host`. Outputs `avg_runtime` each `1h`; alert when `avg_runtime` < 15. Primary focus: Safe Threshold. Purpose-built for 'APC Smart-UPS Battery Runtime Remaining Below Safe Threshold' in Operations workflows.
value: UC-15.1.26 gives Operations teams earlier visibility into Safe Threshold through `snmp:apc:ups` feeds, lowering operational risk and delayed incident response.
implementation: Poll each managed card on a fixed cadence (typically five minutes) via Splunk Connect for SNMP profiles; keep SNMP Modular Input off the same targets to prevent duplicate cadence drift. Harmonize divisor math with `snmpwalk` findings because PowerNet sometimes stores hundredths of a minute—mirror the SPL `eval runtime_min=tonumber(upsAdvBatteryRunTimeRemaining)/6000` pattern only after validation. Pair runtime collapse with `upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator` and `upsAdvBatteryCapacity` before paging. Fire when the one-hour rolling average stays below fifteen minutes while honoring suppression during tagged maintenance.
visualization: Line chart of hourly average runtime per UPS host with optional reference band at fifteen minutes; single-value panel showing worst-affected `host`; table listing hosts under threshold with latest `upsAdvOutputLoad` and replace-indicator columns for operator triage.

references.title: Splunk Documentation: Splunk Connect for SNMP

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `power` (UC-15.1.26)** — Planned work for 'APC Smart-UPS Battery Runtime Remaining Below Safe Threshold' shifts `avg_runtime` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `snmp:apc:ups`** — Scheduled automation elevates `runtime_min` without crossing `avg_runtime` < 15 for UC-15.1.26. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `power` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `snmp:apc:ups`** — First 48h baseline for UC-15.1.26 on `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) workers with SNMPv3 secrets in the credential store and firewall rules permitting UDP/161 from worker subnets to each APC Network Management Card VLAN.
• Lab-only parity may use SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) on a heavy forwarder—avoid dual collectors hitting the same target in production.
• Normalize scaling per firmware: validate raw `upsAdvBatteryRunTimeRemaining` with `snmpwalk` against the LCD; document whether hundredths-of-minute divisors (`/6000`, `/100`, etc.) apply and capture them in a lookup keyed by `host` + firmware.

Indexing and access
• Require events on `index=power` `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups`; scope a dedicated RBAC role (for example `power_ops`, or Splunk Cloud delegated admin) to that index and dependent knowledge objects.

Detection wiring
• Align saved-search windows with the poller cadence from your SC4SNMP profile YAML (commonly 5 minutes): sample pattern `dispatch.earliest_time=-65m@m`, `dispatch.latest_time=now`, `cron_schedule=*/5 * * * *`, suppress on `host`, and throttle duplicates.
• Author validation panels querying `index=power sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups` using `timechart span=1h avg(runtime_min) by host` plus an overlay for `upsAdvOutputLoad` to explain sudden drops.

Runbook hygiene
• Cross-check Splunk averages against the APC web UI and, where deployed, parallel `apcupsd`/`upsc` readings for the same UPS during two maintenance windows.
• After battery swaps, demand two consecutive polls above the guardrail before clearing incidents so SNMP brownouts do not auto-close real faults.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the upstream Splunk app or TA: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266), SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617).

**Expected data sources:** APC Smart-UPS Network Management Card publishes PowerNet-MIB `upsAdvBatteryRunTimeRemaining`; ingestion uses Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) into `index=power` with `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups`. Pair the gauge with extracted siblings such as `upsAdvOutputLoad` and `upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator` to separate load-driven shrink from end-of-life cells. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.

**Indexes referenced by the SPL:** `power`
**Sourcetypes referenced by the SPL:** `snmp:apc:ups`

After enabling the input, confirm event arrival on a search head with:

```spl
index=* sourcetype="snmp:apc:ups" earliest=-15m | head 5
```

Tune the input's polling interval, batch size, and field extraction to match the volume and latency requirements of the alert. Keep an operational baseline of expected events-per-minute so anomalous drops in ingest can be detected separately from anomalous behaviour.


Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Use the SPL on the use-case page as the starting point. Schedule it as a saved search (typically every 5–15 minutes over a rolling lookback equal to the alert's intended detection window). Tune the threshold (`where`/`stats` clauses) to your environment's normal baseline before enabling alert actions. For high-volume sources, use `tstats` against the accelerated data model when possible.

Step 5 — Troubleshoot

Common failure modes for this use case:

• **No events arriving** — Confirm the upstream input on the forwarder or HEC endpoint is enabled and reachable from the data-collection tier. Inspect `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/splunkd.log` for input errors. Cross-check with `| tstats count where index=power sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups earliest=-1h`.

• **Field extraction returning null** — Inspect the relevant `props.conf` / `transforms.conf` for the sourcetype on the search head and indexer. A vendor TA upgrade or a corporate hardening script can break the regex. Compare against the TA's default stanza using `splunk btool props list --debug | grep snmp:apc:ups`.

• **Search returns no rows even when the condition is present** — The role running the search may lack `srchIndexesAllowed` for the underlying index. Run `| rest splunk_server=local /servicesNS/-/-/authorization/roles | search title=`role_name` | table title srchIndexesAllowed`, replacing the role name with the role that owns the saved search.

• **High false-positive rate** — Maintain an exception lookup keyed on the dominant noise field (host, user, src, process_name, etc.) and join it to the alert with `| lookup <exceptions>.csv key OUTPUT in_exceptions | where in_exceptions!="yes"`. Prefer narrow per-key suppressions over wholesale disabling.

• **Alert fires repeatedly during expected maintenance windows** — Maintain a `maintenance_windows` lookup and join it against the alert: `| lookup maintenance_windows host OUTPUT in_window | where in_window!="yes"`. Keep the lookup in source control next to the saved-search definitions.

• **Alert never fires even when the dashboard shows the condition** — The alert's scheduled time range probably doesn't match the search. Verify cron schedule and earliest/latest tokens align with the intended detection window.
